top10.introHtml: Refreshed 2026-08-27. Searched Cars.com (27 total, 17 kept after 4-seat + exclude filters), CarGurus (78 total, 11 kept), AutoTrader (64 total, 21 kept). Excluded as 2-seat: Mercedes SL 500, Ford Thunderbird 2002, Lexus SC 430, Cadillac Allante. Noted as uncertain seat count but included: Pontiac Firebird Trans Am (2+2). TrueCar skipped (body-style filter broken).

picks.whyGood: W209 CLK is one of Mercedes's most elegant convertibles. Only 65k miles at this price is exceptional — these often sell with 120k+. The CLK350's 3.5L V6 is smooth and reliable. Sitting 2 miles from Media makes inspection easy.
picks.whatToVerify: Full top cycle (raise & lower 3x). Check headliner and rear seat carpet for water stains (roof seal weeping). Inspect rocker panels for rust. Check power windows and sunroof (if equipped). CLK-specific: hydraulic top pump, top seals around rear window.
picks.bottomLine: The closest listing, lowest miles, and a known-reliable platform — the easiest yes in this batch.

picks.whyGood: A manual-transmission S550 Mustang convertible 1 mile from home is rare. The 2.3L EcoBoost makes 310hp and gets reasonable MPG. S550 generation (2015+) is a huge leap in refinement over the S197. Premium trim adds leather, nav, and upgraded audio.
picks.whatToVerify: Manual clutch engagement point (high bite = worn clutch). Synchro feel on 2nd and 3rd gear shifts. Throw-out bearing noise at idle. Soft-top full cycle and rear window clarity. Rear seat water staining from top seal. MT-82 gearbox known for notchy shifts — normal, not a defect.
picks.bottomLine: Rare manual Mustang convertible at your doorstep — buy this first if the top is solid.

picks.whyGood: The E46 330Ci convertible with a manual is widely considered one of the best driver's cars BMW ever made. 105k miles is reasonable for the M54 inline-6, which is bulletproof with regular oil changes. The E46 body-in-white is stiffer than the M3's.
picks.whatToVerify: Manual clutch and synchros (especially 2nd). Coolant expansion tank and thermostat housing (common E46 plastics). Oil leaks at valve cover and rear main. Top hydraulic rams (cylinders weep at high mileage). Spring perch rust — lift the rubber seat and inspect. Rear subframe cracks (check underneath).
picks.bottomLine: Best pure driver's car in the batch — a manual E46 330Ci at this price is a steal if the mechanicals are sorted.

picks.whyGood: Great Deal badge at under $10.5k for an F33 428i xDrive. AWD adds year-round confidence. The N20 2.0L turbo is peppy and the F-series interior is a big step up from the E-series. 119k miles is manageable with documented service.
picks.whatToVerify: N20 timing chain and tensioner (known issue on early N20s — check for rattling on cold start). Coolant hose condition. Top hydraulic rams. xDrive transfer case fluid. Check CarFax for any unrecorded accidents.
picks.bottomLine: Great Deal badge + AWD + under $10.5k makes this the best value BMW in the batch.

picks.whyGood: The 2012 GT has the 5.0L Coyote V8 making 412hp — more engine than anything else in this price range. S197 generation is simple, parts are cheap, and the V8 soundtrack is genuinely thrilling. 117k miles is acceptable on the Coyote.
picks.whatToVerify: 3-valve cam phaser rattle does not apply to the 2012 GT (5.0L Coyote is clean). Check for 8.8 rear axle clunk on takeoff. Top latch mechanism — confirm positive latch at both pillars. Rear seat water staining. Spring perch rust (common on S197).
picks.bottomLine: Best bang-for-buck V8 convertible in this budget — if the top is solid, it's a weekend winner.

picks.whyGood: Only 44,625 miles on an E64 650i — that's genuinely exceptional. The N62 4.8L V8 is smooth and powerful. At under $13k with these miles, this is priced like a worn economy car. Grand-tourer character with a back seat.
picks.whatToVerify: N62 Vanos and valve stem seals (very common, can be expensive). SMG transmission if equipped — confirm shifts smoothly. Top hydraulic ram condition. Oil consumption check (quart per 1k mi is acceptable for N62). Interior condition at these miles.
picks.bottomLine: Unicorn mileage for a V8 BMW grand tourer — if the mechanicals are healthy, this is the most car per dollar.

picks.whyGood: The newest car in the batch — a 2020 S550 Mustang. Better IRS rear suspension than the S197, modern infotainment, driver-assist features. Fred Beans is a reputable Langhorne dealer with CarFax available.
picks.whatToVerify: Full top cycle and rear window. Interior for water staining. Confirm EcoBoost or V6 (trim says Premium which fits either). Rear-camera function. MT-82 shift feel if manual.
picks.bottomLine: Most modern car in the batch at this price — strong choice if you want updated technology.

picks.whyGood: Under $7,500 for a 335i convertible with 91k miles — Great Deal badge confirms it's priced below market. The N54 twin-turbo I6 makes 300hp and has enormous tuning potential. At this price, any mechanical investment still keeps you under $10k all-in.
picks.whatToVerify: N54 high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) — critical check. Charge pipe condition. Turbo boost leaks. Cooling system hoses and expansion tank. Top hydraulic rams. Spring perch rust on rear.
picks.bottomLine: Cheapest real driver's car in the batch — budget for HPFP replacement (~$500) and you're still ahead.

picks.whyGood: The B8.5 A5 Cabriolet is one of the best-looking soft tops in the segment. Quattro AWD is a real benefit. Good Deal badge at 111k miles. The 2.0T TFSI is reliable with regular oil changes.
picks.whatToVerify: Timing chain tensioner (early B8s had issues; 2016 B8.5 is improved). Top drain tubes (check for clogs causing water intrusion). DSG fluid service interval. Front control arm bushings at this mileage.
picks.bottomLine: Elegant AWD Audi convertible at a fair price — solid pick if you want quattro and a premium interior.

picks.whyGood: The B8 S5 with the supercharged 3.0L V6 is a phenomenal engine — 333hp with an Audi quattro sound. At 69k miles it's well-broken-in but not worn out. Premium Plus adds most comfort options.
picks.whatToVerify: Supercharger belt and coupler — they wear and are expensive. Carbon buildup on intake valves (common on direct-injection engines). Quattro/Haldex clutch pack fluid. Top drain tubes.
picks.bottomLine: The most powerful Audi in the batch — supercharged V6 convertible under $14k is genuinely good value.

manual10.introHtml: Only 2 confirmed manual-transmission convertibles surfaced across all three sources this refresh. Manual convertibles are extremely scarce in this price/radius combination.

picks.whyGood: S550 EcoBoost with a 6-speed manual 1 mile from Media — modern chassis, 310hp turbo, and a stick shift. Rare combination.
picks.whatToVerify: Clutch engagement point (high = worn). 2nd/3rd synchro smooth shift test. Throw-out bearing chirp at idle. Top full cycle. Rear seat water staining.
picks.bottomLine: Only 1 mile away and the most modern manual convertible in this search — a must-test-drive.

picks.whyGood: The E46 330Ci manual is the benchmark driver's convertible. M54 inline-6, perfectly balanced, legendary handling.
picks.whatToVerify: Clutch engagement. 2nd/3rd synchros. Spring perch rust. Cooling system plastics. Rear subframe mounting points.
picks.bottomLine: The driver's car of the batch — manual E46 330Ci with sorted mechanicals is a 10-year keeper.

mustangs.introHtml: 2005+ Ford Mustang convertibles (S197 and S550 generations) in budget. All picks are EcoBoost or GT trim. Pre-2005 Mustangs excluded per criteria.

picks.whyGood: S550 EcoBoost with 6-speed manual, 1 mile from Media. The S550 generation has proper IRS, excellent interior, and modern safety features. Manual EcoBoost is a fun blend of economy and performance.
picks.whatToVerify: Clutch wear. MT-82 synchros (2nd and 3rd). Top full cycle and rear window clarity. Rear seat water staining. Check CarFax.
picks.bottomLine: Best-in-class S550 manual at your doorstep.

picks.whyGood: Newest Mustang in the batch. S550 with MagneRide if equipped. Fred Beans is a reputable dealer.
picks.whatToVerify: Top latch mechanism. Rear window clarity. Full top cycle. Confirm engine (EcoBoost vs V6). Rear camera.
picks.bottomLine: Newest car, reputable dealer — great option if you prefer automatic S550.

picks.whyGood: S550 automatic from Weathers Motors (same dealer as the manual example). Same miles but $488 cheaper — likely the same car listed on both platforms at different prices.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm if same VIN as CarGurus listing 450114396. Top cycle. All trim features.
picks.bottomLine: Possibly same car as rank #1 but automatic — verify VIN before committing.

picks.whyGood: 2012 GT with 5.0L Coyote V8 — 412hp, proper roar, simple mechanicals. S197 is easy to work on and parts are cheap. Private seller in Broomall (nearby).
picks.whatToVerify: 8.8 rear axle clunk on takeoff. Top latch both pillars. Spring perch rust. Rear seat water staining. Confirm manual or auto.
picks.bottomLine: The V8 Mustang at the top of budget — pure fun if the top is sound.
